We have mass spec data: m/z 193.1103 (base peak). Likely molecular ion. Need to deduce formula. Use typical organic compound. m/z 193.1103 suggests maybe C? Let's calculate possible formulas. Use typical atomic masses: C 12.0000, H 1.007825, O 15.994915, N 14.003074. 193.1103 could be C? Let's try C11H? C11 = 132, need 61.1103 left. If O2 (31.9898) leaves 29.1205, which could be H29? H29 mass ~29.2269, close. So C11H29O2 would be 132+29.2269+31.9898=193.2167, too high. Try C10H? C10=120, left 73.1103. O3 = 47.9847, left 25.1256 ~ H25 (25.1956). So C10H25O3 = 120+25.1956+47.9847=193.1803, a bit high. Try C9H? C9=108, left 85.1103. O4=63.9797, left 21.1306 ~ H21 (21.1643). C9H21O4 =108+21.1643+63.9797=193.144, close. Slight high. Try C8H? C8=96, left 97.1103. O5=79.9746, left 17.1357 ~ H17 (17.1330). C8H17O5 =96+17.133+79.9746=193.1076, very close! So formula likely C8H17O5. DBE = C - H/2 + N/2 +1 = 8 - 17/2 +1 =8 -8.5 +1 =0.5? Not integer, but with O doesn't affect. So maybe not correct. DBE must be integer. So maybe formula includes N. Try C8H15NO5: mass = 96 + 15*1.007825=96+15.1174=111.1174, + N 14.0031 =125.1205, + O5 79.9746 =205.0951 too high. Need 193. So maybe C9H13O5? C9=108, H13=13.1017 =>121.1017, O5=79.9746 =>201.0763 too high. C9H9O4? 108+9.0704=117.0704+63.9797=181.0501 low. C10H13O4? 120+13.1017=133.1017+63.9797=197.0814 high. C9H13O4? 108+13.1017=121.1017+63.9797=185.0814 low. C9H13O5 we did 201. So maybe includes chlorine? Cl isotopic pattern? The mass spec shows isotopic peaks at +1, +2 etc typical for chlorine (Cl 35/37 ratio ~3:1). Here intensities: M+1 12.5% of base, M+2 1.1% etc. That's typical for one chlorine? For chlorine, M+2 about 1/3 of M. Here M+2 intensity 1.1% vs base 100, far lower. So maybe not chlorine. Could be one bromine? M+2 ~ 100% of M. Not. So maybe just natural isotopic distribution of C13 (1.1% per carbon). For 193, M+1 12.5% suggests about 11-12 carbons (since each C adds ~1.1%). So maybe 11 carbons. Let's compute C11H? C11=132, need 61.1103. O2=31.9898 leaves 29.1205 ~ H29 (29.2269) too high. O3=47.9847 leaves 13.1256 ~ H13 (13.1017) close. So C11H13O3 mass =132+13.1017+47.9847=193.0864, a bit low (0.024). Could be C11H15O3: add 2 H =2.01565 =>195.102? Actually 193.0864+2.01565=195.102, too high. So maybe C10H? C10=120, need 73.1103. O4=63.9797 leaves 9.1306 ~ H9 (9.0704) close. So C10H9O4 mass =120+9.0704+63.9797=193.0501 low by 0.06. C10H10O4: +1.0078 =>194.058, too high. So maybe C9H? C9=108, need 85.1103. O5=79.9746 leaves 5.1357 ~ H5 (5.0391) close. C9H5O5 mass =108+5.0391+79.9746=193.0137 low. C9H6O5: +1.0078 =>194.0215 high. So maybe includes nitrogen: C9H9NO3? mass =108+9.0704=117.0704 +14.0031=131.0735 +47.9847=179.0582 low. C9H9NO4: +15.9949 =>195.0531 high. So maybe formula C10H13O3? mass =120+13.1017+47.9847=181.0864 low. C10H13O4 we had 197. So not.

Let's compute exact mass for C11H13O3: using monoisotopic masses: C 12.0000, H 1.007825, O 15.994915. So C11 =132.0000, H13 =13.101725, O3 =47.984745. Sum =193.08647. Observed 193.11028, diff 0.0238 (23 mDa). Could be due to measurement error? Might be okay. But isotopic pattern suggests many carbons (M+1 12.5% ~ 11-12 C). So C11 plausible.

Check C12H? C12=144, need 49.1103. O2=31.9898 leaves 17.1205 ~ H17 (17.1330) close. C12H17O2 mass =144+17.1330+31.9898=193.1228, diff 0.0125 high. M+1 intensity would be ~12*1.1=13.2% matches. So C12H17O2 plausible. DBE = C - H/2 +1 =12 - 8.5 +1 =4.5 not integer. So maybe includes N: C12H17NO? O1=15.9949, N=14.0031 total 30. - compute: 144+17.1330+14.0031+15.9949=191.131, low.

C12H13O3? mass =144+13.1017+47.9847=205.0864 high.

C13H? C13=156, need 37.1103. O1=15.9949 leaves 21.1154 ~ H21 (21.1643) close. C13H21O mass =156+21.1643+15.9949=193.1592 high 0.049.

C13H17O2? 156+17.133+31.9898=205.1228 high.

Thus best match maybe C12H17O2 (mass 193.1228) diff 0.0125 (12.5 mDa). Acceptable? Could be measurement error.

Now need to propose structure. Use NMR data? Not yet measured. Could use carbon and proton NMR to narrow. Let's get carbon NMR.
